result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Choosing, Checking and Reporting" subtitle: "Cross-validation · overfitting · marginal predictions · extrapolation · reporting non-linear effects · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 1 to 4: curves and interactions - Today: **which curve**, **how to check it**, and **how to report it** ::: # Topic 1 — Choosing {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Cross-validated error ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) fold <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(ncd))) cv_rmse <- function(fit_fun) sqrt(mean(sapply(1:10, function(k) { f <- fit_fun(ncd[fold != k, ]); mean((ncd$sbp[fold == k] - predict(f, ncd[fold == k, ]))^2) }))) round(c(linear = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)), hinge = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ age + pmax(age - 45, 0) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)), ns4 = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ ns(age, 4) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d)), gam = cv_rmse(function(d) gam(sbp ~ s(age) + s(bmi) + s(activity) + salt + sex + smoker, data = d, method = "REML")), ns15 = cv_rmse(function(d) lm(sbp ~ ns(age, 15) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, d))), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` linear hinge ns4 gam ns15 11.33 11.27 11.28 11.22 11.29 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **10-fold cross-validation**: fit on 9/10 of the data, **predict the held-out tenth** - Linear **11.33**, hinge **11.27**, spline **11.28**, GAM **11.22**: curved models are **slightly better**; the gains are small because the **noise is large** - **ns with 15 df: 11.29**: **more flexibility did not help**; it fits noise - Choose the **simplest curve that fits** and is easy to explain ::: ## Decision guide | Situation | Suggested approach | |---|---| | Curvature unknown | **GAM** or **ns() with 3 to 5 df**, then plot | | Diminishing returns | **log** transform | | Known threshold or bend | **hinge** at a justified knot | | Small sample | few df (3), or linear and say so | | Report to non-statisticians | **prediction plot**; hinge slopes if simple | | Effect depends on another variable | **interaction**, plus simple slopes and risks | # Topic 2 — Checking and extrapolation {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Marginal (standardised) predictions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g_ns <- glm(cvd10 ~ age + ns(bmi, 4) + sex * smoker, data = ncd, family = binomial) bmis <- c(18.5, 22, 25, 30, 35) round(setNames(100 * sapply(bmis, function(b) mean(predict(g_ns, transform(ncd, bmi = b), type = "response"))), bmis), 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 18.5 22 25 30 35 13.8 6.1 4.7 11.8 39.6 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The **average predicted risk if every adult had that BMI**: **13.8%** at 18.5, **6.1%** at 22, **4.7%** at 25, **11.8%** at 30, **39.6%** at 35. It averages over the **real mix** of age, sex and smoking, so it needs **no "typical person"**. ::: ## Do not extrapolate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} range(ncd$bmi); sum(ncd$bmi > 40) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 14.5 40.1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} BMI ranges from **14.5 to 40.1**, and **one adult** has a BMI above 40. A prediction at BMI 50 is **pure extrapolation** (the natural spline just continues in a straight line). Restrict plots and statements to the **range of the data**, and show where the data are thin (a **rug** or histogram). ::: # Topic 3 — Reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Reporting a non-linear effect ::: {.good} - **A prediction plot** with a **95% band** (and a rug of the data) - A **few contrasts** at meaningful values (e.g. OR for BMI 30 vs 24.6) - The **test of non-linearity** (LR or F test) - The **method**: spline type, **df** (and how chosen), knots - **Never** a table of spline coefficients ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ref <- predict(g_ns, transform(ncd[1, ], bmi = 24.6)) round(setNames(sapply(bmis, function(b) exp(predict(g_ns, transform(ncd[1, ], bmi = b)) - ref)), bmis), 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 18.5 22 25 30 35 3.8 1.4 1.0 3.1 21.5 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} OR compared with a BMI of 24.6: **3.8** (18.5), **1.4** (22), **1.0** (25), **3.1** (30), **21.5** (35): the **shape** is the message, not one odds ratio per unit. ::: ## An example sentence ::: {.key} *"The 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event was U-shaped in BMI (natural spline, 4 df; likelihood-ratio test of non-linearity p < 0.001), lowest between BMI 24 and 25 and rising to 4.7% at BMI 25, 11.8% at 30 and 39.6% at 35 (standardised to the sample)."* ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `curves-workshop/labs/lab5_report.R` - 10-fold cross-validated RMSE, overfitting - marginal predictions and ORs for chosen BMIs - extrapolation check and a one-sentence report ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="409nzk.cayt17" data-show="Q3VydmF0dXJlIGhlbHBzIGEgbGl0dGxlOiBwcmVmZXIgYSBzaW1wbGUgY3VydmUgdW5sZXNz IHRoZSBHQU0gY2xlYXJseSB3aW5z" data-explain="VGhlIGdhaW4gZnJvbSBjdXJ2YXR1cmUgaXMgcmVhbCBidXQgc21hbGwuIEEgc2ltcGxlLCBl eHBsYWluYWJsZSBjdXJ2ZSBpcyBwcmVmZXJyZWQgdW5sZXNzIGEgbW9yZSBjb21wbGV4IG1v ZGVsIGlzIGNsZWFybHkgYmV0dGVyLg=="} Cross-validated RMSE is 11.33 (linear), 11.27 (hinge), 11.28 (spline) and 11.22 (GAM). What is the most sensible conclusion? - The GAM is best, since it has the lowest RMSE of the four models compared here - The linear model is best, since it has the fewest parameters of all the models - The data are unusable, since all the differences are smaller than 0.1 mmHg - Curvature helps a little: prefer a simple curve unless the GAM clearly wins ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="40a186.caz7ih" data-show="SXQgZm9sbG93cyB0aGUgbm9pc2UgaW4gdGhlIHNhbXBsZSBhbmQgcHJlZGljdHMgbmV3IGRh dGEgbm8gYmV0dGVy" data-explain="VG9vIG11Y2ggZmxleGliaWxpdHkgZml0cyByYW5kb20gdmFyaWF0aW9uLCB3aGljaCBkb2Vz IG5vdCByZXBlYXQgaW4gbmV3IGRhdGEuIFRoZSBjcm9zcy12YWxpZGF0ZWQgZXJyb3IgaXMg bm8gYmV0dGVyIHRoYW4gd2l0aCA0IGRmLg=="} Why is a natural spline for age with 15 df a poor choice? - It follows the noise in the sample and predicts new data no better - It cannot be fitted when there are fewer than 15 distinct ages - It makes the model non-linear in the coefficients, so least squares fails - It removes the age effect by splitting it across many terms ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="40aegx.cazlzw" data-show="VGhlIGF2ZXJhZ2UgcHJlZGljdGVkIHJpc2sgaWYgZXZlcnkgYWR1bHQgaW4gdGhlIHNhbXBs ZSBoYWQgYSBCTUkgb2YgMzA=" data-explain="U2V0IEJNSSB0byAzMCBmb3IgZXZlcnlib2R5LCBwcmVkaWN0IGZvciBlYWNoIGFkdWx0IHdp dGggdGhlaXIgb3duIGFnZSwgc2V4IGFuZCBzbW9raW5nLCBhbmQgYXZlcmFnZS4gTm8gc2lu Z2xlIHR5cGljYWwgcGVyc29uIGlzIG5lZWRlZC4="} What is a marginal (standardised) predicted risk at BMI 30? - The predicted risk of the adult who has the median BMI of the sample - The observed risk among the adults who happen to have a BMI of around 30 - The average predicted risk if every adult in the sample had a BMI of 30 - The predicted risk when every other variable in the model is set to zero ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="40arpl.cb00h8" data-show="VGhlcmUgYXJlIGFsbW9zdCBubyBkYXRhIHRoZXJlLCBzbyB0aGUgY3VydmUgaXMganVzdCBh biBleHRyYXBvbGF0aW9u" data-explain="QmV5b25kIHRoZSBkYXRhIHRoZSBmaXR0ZWQgY3VydmUgaXMgZGV0ZXJtaW5lZCBieSB0aGUg Zm9ybSBvZiB0aGUgc3BsaW5lLCBub3QgYnkgb2JzZXJ2YXRpb25zLiBTdGF5IHdpdGhpbiB0 aGUgb2JzZXJ2ZWQgcmFuZ2UgYW5kIHNob3cgd2hlcmUgZGF0YSBhcmUgdGhpbi4="} Why is it unwise to predict the risk at BMI 50 when only one adult has a BMI above 40? - The standard errors are zero outside the range of the data in the survey - There are almost no data there, so the curve is just an extrapolation - The spline cannot be evaluated outside the range of the knots it uses - Predictions are limited to BMI values in the lowest quartile of the data ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="40b4yb.cb0eym" data-show="QSBwcmVkaWN0aW9uIHBsb3Qgd2l0aCBhIENJIGJhbmQsIGFuZCBhIGZldyBjb250cmFzdHMg YXQgc2V0IHZhbHVlcw==" data-explain="U3BsaW5lIGNvZWZmaWNpZW50cyBjYW5ub3QgYmUgcmVhZCBvbmUgYnkgb25lIGFuZCBhIHNp bmdsZSBPUiBoaWRlcyB0aGUgc2hhcGUuIEEgcGxvdCwgYSBmZXcgY29udHJhc3RzIGFuZCB0 aGUgdGVzdCBvZiBub24tbGluZWFyaXR5IGNvbnZleSB0aGUgcmVzdWx0Lg=="} What is the best way to report a non-linear effect? - The p-value of each one of the spline coefficients, listed in a table - A single odds ratio per unit of BMI taken from the straight-line model - A prediction plot with a CI band, and a few contrasts at set values - The degrees of freedom of the spline, together with its AIC value in a table ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Cross-validate** and prefer the **simplest** adequate curve - More df = **overfitting** - **Standardised predictions** need no typical person - **Do not extrapolate**; show where the data are - Report **plot + contrasts + non-linearity test + df** ::: **Next:** Cheat sheet and the next module

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
